back: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
A magnetic material becoming a magnet when placed near or touching a magnet.
Soft iron: easily magnetised and demagnetised (temporary magnets). Steel: harder to magnetise but keeps it (permanent magnets).
A region where a magnetic pole feels a force; its direction is the force on a north pole.

front: Field lines around a bar magnet?
back: From N to S outside the magnet; closer lines mean a stronger field.

front: The only sure test for a magnet?
back: Repulsion: one end repels a pole of a known magnet.
Magnetise: stroking, or d.c. in a solenoid. Demagnetise: heating, hammering, or a.c. in a solenoid while withdrawing slowly.
